headline: How do I get my kid off the game without a fight?
description: Count matches, not minutes. How to end a game session without a fight: what to ask before your kid starts, what to say at the end, and what to do if it blows up.

itemListElement.name: How do I get my kid off the game without a fight?

mainEntity.name: Should I give a five-minute warning before my kid gets off the game?

acceptedAnswer.text: For team games, usually not. Ten minutes into a 45-minute League match, "five minutes left" means nothing, because the match can't end in five. Ask how long the match has left, or agree before they start that this is the last one. For games without matches, like Minecraft, a warning to get to a save point works.

mainEntity.name: What if my kid says they can't pause the game?

acceptedAnswer.text: They're probably right. An online team match keeps going without them, the same as a soccer or basketball game. If your kid were on the court, you wouldn't pull them off mid-game. You'd wait for the whistle. Agree to stop at the end of the match, and agree before they start that no new match begins after the number you set.

mainEntity.name: How many matches should I let my kid play?

acceptedAnswer.text: Start with the time you have, then turn it into matches. An hour is one or two League games, two Marvel Rivals matches, or plenty of Smash. Talk it through before they start, so the number is set before the first match.

mainEntity.name: Is it OK to take away video games as a punishment?

acceptedAnswer.text: That's your call. If you do, the AAP suggests enforcing limits "supportively rather than punitively." Before it gets there, lean in. Most of these fights come from the distance between what you expected and what they expected.

mainEntity.name: How do I get my kid off Minecraft or Roblox?

acceptedAnswer.text: Agree on a stopping point the game understands before they start: a save point, the next nightfall in Minecraft, or the end of a round in a Roblox game. Ask "does this save?" so stopping doesn't cost their progress. Try to understand what they're building before you judge the screen time, and the stop gets easier to agree on.
